subject: URGENT: Customer checkout failures tied to client prefetch merging
messages:
From: Caroline Dunn <caroline@fastcart.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-05T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: (no subject)

Hi Lauren —

We started seeing a spike in checkout failures this morning around 08:45 PDT. P99 latency for the Redwood streaming calls that power our checkout summary has jumped from ~120ms to >2.1s and a subset of requests are returning truncated payloads or 500s. This is directly impacting conversion on our busiest flow.

We're using the client SDK v1.4.2 with prefetch enabled. I attached a screenshot of the front-end error rates and a short server trace where you can see the stream cut mid-header.

Attachments: screenshot_20260905.png (image/png), prefetch_trace.log (text/plain)

Can your team triage? We need a workaround ASAP — even turning off streaming on our side temporarily is an option if you recommend it.

Thanks,
Caroline
Head of Engineering, FastCart

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Caroline Dunn <caroline@fastcart.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-05T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Customer checkout failures tied to client prefetch merging

Hi Caroline — thanks for the quick flag and the logs. I’m escalating to our infra/SDK team and looping in Karthik and Monica for immediate triage.

Immediate asks:
- Karthik/Monica: can you confirm whether prefetch merging in client v1.4.2 can cause interleaved frame/header corruption? Caroline attached a trace that looks like header bytes split across frames.
- Caroline: if you can switch the checkout route to the non-streaming endpoint for the next 30–60 minutes, please do that as a mitigation while we investigate. If that’s not possible, we’ll provide a scoped hotfix.

I’ll update FastCart within the hour with next steps.

—Lauren
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: 2026-09-05T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Customer checkout failures tied to client prefetch merging

Quick triage notes (initial):
- I loaded the prefetch_trace.log Caroline provided. The pattern looks like a race when the client SDK merges prefetched frames with live frames during assembly. We see header blobs split mid-field which leads our parser to treat the payload as malformed and drop the connection, returning a 500 on the server side when the stream reassembly fails.
- This specifically reproduces with client SDK v1.4.2 when prefetch+merge is enabled and concurrent requests overlap on the same socket (heavy checkout traffic).
- Short-term mitigation: disable prefetch merging on the client. I’ve attached a small patch that adds an env flag to opt out (hotfix_disable_prefetch.patch). Recommend instructing FastCart to flip the flag immediately. That should reduce the interleaving and restore stability.

Longer-term: we should push a client SDK release that:
1) adds stronger frame boundary checks to the streaming parser,
2) makes prefetch merges atomic per-request (avoid cross-request concat),
3) adds more conservative backpressure when prefetch buffer is non-empty.

I’ll prepare a canary build if we want to ship a fix today.

Karthik
Lead, Inference SDK
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-05T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Executive note: FastCart production impact — request for urgent patch + credit approval

Markus —

Summary: FastCart (large retail customer) has a production incident causing checkout failures (p99 >2s, intermittent 500s). Root cause (triage by SDK infra): a prefetch-chunk merge race in client SDK v1.4.2 that can corrupt streaming headers under high parallelism. Karthik has a short-term opt-out patch that disables prefetch merging and a proposed code fix for a canary ship.

Impact: increased checkout abandonment; FastCart is reporting a 4.8% drop in conversions on affected sessions. They are asking for an immediate fix and compensation conversation.

Ask: approve the following so we can act now —
- Permission to push a canary SDK build (hotfix) to FastCart and any other customers on v1.4.2 with prefetch enabled.
- Approval to offer a one-week service credit and a joint postmortem and remediation plan.

I’ll coordinate the customer comms and a timeline for rollout. If approved, Karthik will lead the technical patch; Monica will drive support/CS communication.

—Lauren
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-05T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Executive note: FastCart production impact — request for urgent patch + credit approval

Thanks — marking this as exec-approved for the actions below (we’ve spoken to CS already and they recommend the one-week credit; Legal is ready with a standard statement).

Operational plan we’ll execute now:
- 16:55 PDT: Ask FastCart to flip prefetch opt-out flag (we’ll provide the env var and instructions).
- 17:15 PDT: If opt-out is insufficient, we’ll deploy Karthik’s canary SDK to a FastCart dev shard and roll to prod after 30m validation.
- Tonight: Open postmortem ticket (INF-3241) with owner Karthik + timeline for the SDK release (target: patch release 1.4.3 in 72 hours).

I’ll update Caroline directly and include the support playbook. Thanks for the quick loop — we should also notify account exec to keep commercial folks aligned on credit language.

—Monica
Director, Customer Reliability
monica_patel@redwood.ai
